Accountable for establishing Scrum and for the Scrum Team's effectiveness. 'True leaders who serve' the team and the organization.
One person, not a committee. Accountable for maximizing the product's value and for Product Backlog management. Can delegate the work but stays accountable.
Emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product. The single source of work. Commitment: the Product Goal.
One Scrum Master, one Product Owner and Developers. Typically 10 or fewer people. No sub-teams or hierarchies.
A usable step toward the Product Goal that meets the Definition of Done. Several can be created in one Sprint, and an Increment may be delivered to stakeholders before the Sprint ends.
Fixed-length event of one month or less. The container for all other events. A Sprint could be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete; only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel it.

People outside the Scrum Team with an interest in the product. Key stakeholders are invited to the Sprint Review. Those wanting to change the Product Backlog do so by trying to convince the Product Owner.
Scrum defines only the parts needed to implement its theory. Teams add their own practices around it; implementing only parts of Scrum is possible, but the result is not Scrum.
Learning from experience: decide based on what you observe, not on predictions. One of Scrum's two foundations, with lean thinking.
Reduce waste and focus on the essentials. The second foundation of Scrum.
Pillar 2 of empiricism. Artifacts and progress are checked frequently to spot problems. Without transparency it is 'misleading and wasteful'.
Pillar 3 of empiricism. Adjust as soon as possible when something is off. Inspection without adaptation is 'pointless'.
Pillar 1 of empiricism. The process and work must be visible to those doing it and receiving it. Exam trap: transparency is a pillar, not a value.
The team internally decides who does what, when and how. Replaced the older term 'self-organizing'.
The five Scrum values. Learn them by heart: transparency, trust and collaboration are NOT on this list.
Everyone in the Scrum Team who creates any part of the usable Increment. Not just programmers. Older guides said 'Development Team'.
The long-term objective for the Scrum Team, kept in the Product Backlog. One at a time: fulfill or abandon it before taking on the next.
The team as a whole has all the skills needed to create value each Sprint. Not every person needs every skill.
Fixed-length events of one month or less. The container for all other events. The next Sprint starts immediately after the previous one ends.
The 2020 Guide talks about three accountabilities (Developers, Product Owner, Scrum Master) instead of 'roles'.
Sprint Goal (why) + selected items (what) + actionable plan (how). A plan by and for the Developers, updated throughout the Sprint.
The quality standard for the Increment. Work that doesn't meet it isn't part of the Increment, can't be released or even presented at the Sprint Review.
The single objective for the Sprint, defined by the whole Scrum Team in Sprint Planning. A commitment by the Developers. Fixed goal, flexible scope.
Second-to-last event. A working session with key stakeholders to inspect the outcome and decide what's next. Not a sign-off. Max 4 h for a one-month Sprint.
Anything blocking the team's progress. The Scrum Master 'causes the removal' of impediments, which doesn't mean fixing everything personally.
A maximum duration. One-month Sprint: Sprint Planning 8 h, Sprint Review 4 h, Sprint Retrospective 3 h; for shorter Sprints these events are usually shorter. The Daily Scrum is always 15 minutes.
Starts the Sprint. Three topics: Why (Sprint Goal), What (selected items), How (the plan). Max 8 h for a one-month Sprint. The whole Scrum Team attends.
Concludes the Sprint. Plans ways to increase quality and effectiveness. Max 3 h for a one-month Sprint. Improvements may go into the next Sprint Backlog.
Optional forecasting tools. Useful, but they don't replace empiricism. Not a Scrum artifact.
Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint. A Sprint could be cancelled if its Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
15 minutes for the Developers, every working day, same time and place. Purpose: inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog. No mandatory 'three questions'.
Each artifact has one: Product Backlog = Product Goal, Sprint Backlog = Sprint Goal, Increment = Definition of Done.
An ongoing activity, not an event: breaking items down and adding detail, order and size. The old '10% of capacity' rule is gone in 2020.
Done by the Developers who will do the work. The Product Owner may influence them by helping them understand and select trade-offs.
Scrum's rules can't be changed. You can use only parts of Scrum, but then it isn't Scrum.
